Evolution through Natural Selection is a process where organisms with traits better suited to their environment tend to survive and reproduce more than those less adapted, leading over generations to changes within populations or species.

Charles Darwin proposed this idea after observing variations among individuals of various plant and animal groups during his voyage on the HMS Beagle in 1831. He noticed that some creatures had characteristics giving them an advantage for survival under specific conditions—like thicker fur helping animals survive colder climates, better camouflage aiding prey to avoid predators more effectively.

Individuals with advantageous traits are likelier pass these beneficial attributes onto their offspring through reproduction—a process Darwin termed 'inheritance.' Over time and many generations, such inherited advantages accumulate within a population. This gradual change in the genetic makeup of populations results from differential survival rates among individuals due to varying environmental pressures or challenges they face daily.

Natural Selection thus drives evolution by favoring traits that enhance an organism's ability to survive and reproduce under given conditions—leading species gradually adapt over time, resulting in new forms emerging while others may become extinct. This mechanism explains the diversity of life observed on Earth today as well as its continuous adaptation through millions upon millions years.

A phenomenon known as quantum entanglement occurs when particles become interconnected and instantaneously affect each other, regardless of distance.

Because this connection defies classical physics' limitations on speed-of-light communication constraints, it challenges our understanding of reality itself.

Coherence between these linked states means that measuring one particle's properties instantly determines the other's state in a correlated manner. 

Despite its counterintuitive nature and Einstein’s famous phrase "spooky action at a distance," entanglement has been experimentally verified countless times since John Bell formulated his inequalities over fifty years ago.

Entangled particles thus provide profound insights into quantum mechanics, paving ways for revolutionary technologies like quantum computing that promise to transform our technological landscape.

TCP(Transmission Control Protocol)와 UDP(User Datagram Protocol)는 네트워크에서 데이터 전송을 위한 두 가지 다른 프로토콜입니다.

TCP은 연결 기반 프로토콜이며, 데이터를 정확하게 전송하기 위해 연결이 설정되고 유지됩니다. TCP는 오류를 감지하고 수정하며, 데이터 패킷의 순서를 보장합니다. 이를 통해 TCP은 신뢰할 수 있는 통신을 위해 사용되며, 예를 들어 웹 브라우징(HTTP), 이메일 전송(E-mail), 파일 다운로드와 같은 작업에 적합합니다.

UDP는 연결 기반 프로토콜이 아니며, 데이터 패킷의 순서를 보장하지 않습니다. UDP는 빠르게 데이터를 전송할 수 있도록 설계되어 오류 감지 및 수정 없이 작동합니다. 이는 실시간 응용 프로그램(예: 스트리밍 비디오, 게임)과 같은 작업에 적합한 프로토콜입니다.

요약하자면, TCP은 정확성과 신뢰성이 중요하며, UDP는 속도와 효율성이 중요합니다.
